subject: Clarify: data-use assurances, derivative rights, and EU transfer approach
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsphere.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: MedSphere Legal <legal@medsphere.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify training opt-out / ownership / transfers

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for yesterday's demo — our security and legal teams asked me to follow up with a few contract-level clarifications before we get to signature. Attached is our DPA redline (MedSphere_DPA_redline_20261122.pdf). High-level asks: 

- A hard commitment that customer data (prompts, responses, documents) will not be used to improve or train models unless we give explicit opt-in per contract (no implicit "improve" clause).
- Clear ownership language: MedSphere retains ownership of prompts and outputs and Redwood will not claim derivative/model IP over customer outputs.
- Evidence of subprocessors (EU-based processing), and confirmation of lawful transfer mechanism (SCCs / DTA / UK addendum) for inference/ops telemetry.
- Retention windows and the ability to request an export/audit package proving deletion.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these items, and if so what evidence we can provide (attestations, exported logs, subprocessor list + dates)? We have a tight timeline; looking to close by Dec 10.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: MedSphere_DPA_redline_20261122.pdf

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsphere.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-23T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify training opt-out / ownership / transfers

Elena — thanks for the redline and clear asks. We can accommodate the high-level commitments you listed but will need to confirm precise contract language and evidence scope with Legal + Ops. Quick summary of our proposed approach:

• "No-model-improvement" commitment: a contract clause that prevents Redwood from using customer-provided prompts/responses for model training or fine-tuning unless explicitly authorized. We can offer an exception for aggregated telemetry that is irreversibly anonymized (metrics only) — or omit that entirely if you prefer.

• Ownership / derivative rights: we'll propose language granting customers exclusive ownership of prompts and generated outputs and a unilateral covenant from Redwood not to assert rights over those outputs for model training.

• Subprocessors + transfers: we maintain a published subprocessor list (link below) and can supply dated attestations for subprocessors engaged for your account. For EU transfers, we can execute SCCs and, where required, a UK Addendum.

• Evidence & audits: ops can produce an "audit package" (access logs, deletion attestations, delivery of export) on request; we'll need to scope the package (time range, log granularity) and frequency.

I'm looping in Laura and Rishi to put together contract text and an ops-level checklist. Can you confirm whether MedSphere needs an on-prem or VPC deployment (we offer Private) versus hosted with contractual protections? That affects the transfer mechanics.

Next steps: Laura will propose clause text, Rishi will outline the audit/export content, and I will coordinate DocuSign and timeline.

Best,
Aditya

Attachments: redwood-proposed-clause-draft.txt
Related: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors-list

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsphere.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-24T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify training opt-out / ownership / transfers

Elena / team — drafting notes from Legal below (suggested contract clauses and evidence scope). Please treat as draft language to be negotiated: 

1) No-model-improvement / training exclusion
Proposed clause (short): "Provider shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, attachments, or model outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider's models or underlying model weights, whether directly or indirectly, without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Ownership / derivative rights
Proposed clause (short): "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and Generated Outputs. Provider hereby assigns and waives any rights in Generated Outputs, and agrees not to assert ownership or use Generated Outputs for model training absent Customer's written authorization."

3) Subprocessors & transfers - We will provide a dated subprocessor list and commit to notify you of material additions 30 days in advance.
- For EU data transfers, offer to execute standard contractual clauses (SCCs) and incorporate a Transfer Addendum where required. If MedSphere requires, we can also offer a Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment to avoid cross-border transfer concerns.

4) Evidence and audit package
- Scope: access logs (user, timestamp, action), model-routing records (which model variant served), deletion attestations for specified retention windows.
- Delivery: encrypted archive via secure link or SFTP; include subprocessor attestations where available.

We should also add an operational control: a per-account "model-improvement opt-out" flag enforced at request-routing; this prevents data from entering telemetry and long-term stores. Rishi and Priya — can you confirm technical feasibility and retention windows?

Laura
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
Company: Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsphere.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify training opt-out / ownership / transfers

Quick ops details from my side:

- Opt-out enforcement: we can implement a per-tenant flag that blocks ingestion to analytics/model-improvement pipelines in the routing layer. Flagging will also stop persistent KV cache writes beyond the configured session lifetime.
- Retention: default hosted retention is 30 days for request logs and 90 days for infrastructure traces; for contract we can offer 30/30 (30 days logs + 30 days traces) or a tailored window.
- Audit package content: request export.zip containing (1) access log CSV (timestamp, request_id, route, model_variant, actor), (2) deletion attestations, (3) subprocessor engagement table with contract dates (best-effort), (4) scope-limited infrastructure config snapshot. We'll encrypt with your public key.
- Evidence cadence: one-off on-demand exports are possible; quarterly attestations available as a paid add-on.

Attachment: ops-audit-sample.zip (sample structure).

If MedSphere is particularly sensitive about transfers, recommend Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated hosts in EU region — eliminates the SCC conversation for inference data processed inside EU.

Rishi
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsphere.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify training opt-out / ownership / transfers

Elena — summary and proposed next steps:

1) Contract language: Laura attached the draft clauses (see earlier). We propose the exact no-train and ownership wording above; we can remove the "aggregated telemetry" exception if you prefer an absolute prohibition.

2) Evidence: Ops will prepare the audit package on request. For initial close we can provide: dated subprocessor list, sample audit package, and a deletion attestation for the evaluation period.

3) Transfers: we will execute SCCs for EU transfers. If you need Private deployment in EU, we can get pricing and timeline (typically 3–6 weeks depending on size).

4) Timeline: if MedSphere confirms contract language by Dec 3 we can target DocuSign by Dec 7 and deliver initial evidence by Dec 10.

Please confirm whether you want the absolute no-train clause (no exceptions) or allow anonymized telemetry for product improvement. Also confirm whether you require SCCs + UK Addendum or will accept SCCs alone.

DocuSign link (proposed): https://docusign.example.com/abc123

Best,
Aditya

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsphere.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: MedSphere Legal <legal@medsphere.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify training opt-out / ownership / transfers

Aditya / team — thanks, that plan works. A few quick notes:

- We require an absolute no-train commitment (no telemetry exception).
- Please provide the full subprocessor list with engagement dates and the SCCs + UK Addendum.
- We'll sign once we receive the dated subprocessor list and the sample audit package.

I'll review the draft clauses and follow up with any minor language tweaks (mostly around the ownership clause to be explicit about derivatives). Timeline: aiming for DocuSign by Dec 7 — please send the updated package by Dec 3.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: (none)
